name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A motorcycle, including a motor scooter, with a motor of no more than 5 horsepower (about 3,750 W). An electric two-wheeler that goes faster than a motor scooter's 30 mph but stays within that power is a motor-driven cycle, licensed like a motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle: a saddle the rider sits astride and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces no more than 5 horsepower (about 3,750 W) (Rhode Island General Laws §31-1-3(o))
Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle (M) endorsement, which requires being 16 or older and completing a CCRI motorcycle safety course
Riders under 21, and every rider in the first year after their motorcycle license is issued, must wear an approved helmet
Riders must wear approved eye protection
